In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding the mechanisms that control the shape changes of individual cells and how they coordinate to generate tissue deformations during development.
the role of endocytosis in cell morphogenesis and tissue deformations.
understanding how cells and tissues behave during morphogenesis, and how this process is regulated at the level of individual subcellular processes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
endocytosis is important for apical constriction and recycling is important for cell elongation and tissue elongation.
endocytosis is necessary in the AS to promote apical constriction and that recycling is required in the epidermal cells to promote cell elongation.
“The balance between endocytic and recycling endosomes modulate cell shape changes and tissue behaviour during morphogenesis in Drosophilae”.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
endocytosis is used for membrane retrieval and recycling for membrane addition.
endocytic and recycling endosomes play a key role in the modulation of cell shape changes and tissue deformations that occurs during dorsal closure in Drosophilia.

endocytosis is used to remove membrane during the apical constriction of the AS cells, while recycling is used to add membrane during the cell elongation of the epidermis, and that both processes are essential for tissue morphogenesis.
The main takeaway from our work is that
endocytic and recycling endosomes modulate cell shape changes and tissue behaviour during morphogenesis in Drosophilia.

the modulation of sub-cellular activities is important to regulate tissue morphogenetic processes, and in particular that the balance between endo- and exo-cytosis is important to regulate cell shape changes and tissue behaviour during morphogenesis.

endocytosis is essential for the apical constriction of the amnioserosa during dorsal closure, but not for the cell elongation of the epidermis, while recycling is essential for the cell elongations in both tissues.
